title: systemd backend generates broken ExecStart when command includes shell wrapper
close_reason: Fixed render_exec_start to preserve full /bin/sh -c payload (including appended command tokens), and added regression tests in crates/skdlr-core/src/backend/mod.rs.

title: skdlr logs returns empty for launchd schedules
description:
When using the launchd backend on macOS, `skdlr logs <name>` returns "No runs recorded" even though the scheduled jobs are executing successfully (visible in /tmp/*.log files).

Root cause:
1. launchd runs the skdlr-plist commands directly via the system scheduler — the commands execute and write to stdout/stderr log files, so runs _are happening_.
2. But skdlr's SQLite `runs` table is never populated for these runs. The `InternalBackend.execute_command()` and `Scheduler.handle_success/failure()` both call `storage.save_run()`, while the launchd backend's `run_now()` creates a `Run` with no completion info and `get_runs()` always returns `Vec::new()`.
3. CLI `handle_logs()` queries SQLite first, then falls back to `backend.get_runs()` — but launchd.get_runs() is a no-op.

Also found while investigating:
4. The launchd plist generates invalid `*/15` as an integer value for `StartCalendarInterval`. launchd requires separate dictionaries or comma-separated integers, not a cron-style interval string.

5. The generated plist uses `/bin/sh -c` but wraps with zsh anyway, and launchd's environment is stripped (no PATH from user's shell), so commands like `atuin` fail with "command not found".

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] `skdlr logs <name>` returns actual execution history for launchd-scheduled jobs
- [ ] Plist generation normalizes cron expressions to launchd-compatible format (StartCalendarInterval)
- [ ] Plist generation includes user's PATH in EnvironmentVariables so commands like `atuin` resolve

title: Systemd manual run records duplicate history and add records phantom run
description: Dogfood proof after scheduling oqto-pi-runtime-update: creating/enabling the timer at 06:51:28 produced a succeeded run row even though OnCalendar next trigger was 12:17; one manual skdlr run at 06:51:41 produced two distinct succeeded rows. Native service executed once. Trace run accounting between CLI run_now, systemd service hooks, and journal reconstruction; establish exactly one durable Run per native execution and zero runs on install/enable. Add regression/integration coverage and verify skdlr logs matches journal execution count.
close_reason: Deduplicated storage-backed manual runs against native journal executions using schedule identity and a two-second start-time correlation window; added regression test. Real logs now show exactly two executions (expected Persistent=true catch-up at timer creation plus one manual run), not three. The immediate first execution was confirmed as intended systemd Persistent catch-up, not a phantom run.

title: Container-native multi-user scheduler mode (central schedule authority + per-user execution)
description:
Context
- Current Linux default favors systemd backend and per-user systemd timers.
- For Docker/K8s multi-user runtime, systemd assumptions are a poor fit.
- We want to keep strong per-user isolation while ensuring reliable schedule triggering.

Goal
- Add a container-native runtime mode where skdlr is the central scheduling authority and jobs execute in per-user runtime containers.

Scope
1) Add long-running skdlr-service daemon using internal backend loop (not CLI-driven).
2) Add tenant-safe data model:
   - require tenant/user on schedules
   - unique constraint (tenant_id, name) instead of global name uniqueness.
3) Add job instance/lease model in SQLite:
   - queued/running/succeeded/failed states
   - lease_until, attempts, idempotency_key
   - atomic claim + retry/backoff.
4) Add dispatcher abstraction for execution targets (per-user runner endpoint/token).
5) Add API endpoints for schedule CRUD, run history, pause/resume, and dispatch status.
6) Enforce sandboxing contract:
   - skdlr never executes untrusted host commands in multi-user mode
   - all execution delegated to per-user container runtime/sandbox wrapper.
7) Runtime-mode docs:
   - host-systemd mode (existing)
   - container mode (new)
   - explicit constraints and migration notes.

Acceptance criteria
- In container mode, no loginctl/systemctl dependency in scheduling path.
- Single scheduler authority reliably fires due jobs with no duplicate executions beyond at-least-once semantics.
- Per-user execution remains isolated to user containers.
- Clear operational docs for Docker now, K8s-ready extension later.

title: Build skdlr-service daemon that continuously runs internal scheduler loop
Schema: add tenant_id and change unique key to (tenant_id, name)
Schema: add job_instances lease/retry table for queued/running/succeeded/failed states
Scheduler core: implement atomic claim + lease renewal + stuck-job recovery
close_reason: atomic claim, lease renewal, stuck-job recovery

title: Scheduler core: implement retry/backoff/dead-letter semantics with idempotency keys
Dispatcher: add runner dispatch interface (transport-agnostic, no direct host exec in multi-user mode)
API: implement schedule CRUD + run history + pause/resume endpoints with tenant scoping
Docs: runtime-mode guide (host-systemd vs container mode) and migration notes
Tests: multi-tenant isolation, duplicate-delivery idempotency, retry/lease behavior
oqto fit: sandboxing, remote runners, embedding surface
description:
Make skdlr a first-class scheduling backend for oqto, with structured sandbox handoff, remote runner dispatch, and a clean library/API embedding surface (no more CLI text scraping).

## Context

Today oqto integrates with skdlr by shelling out to the `skdlr` CLI and parsing text output (see oqto_refactor backend/crates/oqto/src/api/handlers/misc.rs:200-400). The integration works for basic scheduling but blocks every direction oqto is heading:

- oqto has a real layered sandbox (oqto-sandbox: bubblewrap/sandbox-exec, oqto-guard FUSE, eavs network proxy, planned seccomp via oqto-cxxr). skdlr only has a generic `executor.wrapper` CLI hook, with config passed via the `SKDLR_OCTO_MODE` env var and `{name}/{workdir}` argv placeholders. That contract won't carry deny/allow lists, network policy, or resource caps.
- oqto already has a runner protocol (RunnerHello over Unix socket / WebSocket, runner_id routing, planned mTLS in oqto-e067, planned SSH bootstrap in oqto-wdkj). skdlr's Dispatcher trait exists with comments anticipating "HTTP-based dispatch to per-user runner agents" but only ships `LocalDispatcher`.
- oqto needs live job logs and per-job timeouts; skdlr persists a `log_path` after the fact and has no per-job timeout.
- Schedule.env stores secrets as plain strings; oqto wants secrets resolved at exec time via eavs.

This epic does NOT reimplement oqto's sandbox inside skdlr — it formalizes the handoff so skdlr stays lean and oqto stays in charge of isolation policy.

## Scope (children)

1. Typed SandboxSpec on Schedule + structured wrapper handoff
2. `runner_selector` + `RemoteDispatcher` trait impl
3. Per-job timeout + resource limits across backends
4. Secrets references decoupled from `env` map
5. Live log streaming endpoint for JobInstance
6. Migrate oqto integration from CLI scraping to skdlr-core library (or stabilized skdlr-api)

## Non-goals

- Reimplementing oqto's sandbox primitives inside skdlr (bwrap, seccomp, FUSE guard stay in oqto-sandbox)
- Building a new transport; reuse oqto's runner channel where possible
- Replacing skdlr-vq7g (durable execution) — this epic depends on its lease/idempotency primitives but does not duplicate them

## Definition of done

- oqto compiles against skdlr-core directly, no CLI parsing
- A schedule can carry a SandboxSpec that round-trips through storage and is delivered to the wrapper as structured JSON
- A schedule can be pinned to a runner_id (or tag set) and dispatched there with lease semantics intact
- Per-job timeout enforced and surfaced in Run/JobInstance
- oqto can stream live stdout/stderr from a running JobInstance
- Docs updated: integration guide for embedders, sandbox contract, runner protocol

title: Typed SandboxSpec on Schedule + structured wrapper handoff
description:
Replace the ad-hoc `executor.wrapper` + `SKDLR_OCTO_MODE` env-var contract with a typed, persisted `SandboxSpec` field on `Schedule`, delivered to the wrapper as structured JSON instead of argv string-stuffing.

## Why

oqto's sandbox is layered (bubblewrap/sandbox-exec, oqto-guard FUSE, eavs network proxy) and configured via rich data: deny_read paths, allow_write paths, isolate_network/pid, profile name, per-workspace overrides. None of that fits today's wrapper contract:

- `executor.wrapper` (crates/skdlr-core/src/config.rs:142) takes a binary + argv with `{name}/{workdir}` placeholders only.
- `SKDLR_OCTO_MODE` env var (validated in `ExecutorConfig::validate()`) is a boolean nudge, not a payload.
- `Schedule` has no field for sandbox config, so per-job overrides have nowhere to live.

Result: oqto can only pass the schedule name + cwd to its wrapper, and any sandbox decision must be made out-of-band (file lookups, env state). That breaks per-job overrides and any audit trail.

## What

### Data model

Add to `Schedule` (crates/skdlr-core/src/models.rs):
```rust
pub sandbox: Option<SandboxSpec>,
```

```rust
pub struct SandboxSpec {
    pub profile: Option<String>,           // named profile resolved by wrapper
    pub deny_read: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub allow_read: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub deny_write: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub allow_write: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub isolate_network: Option<NetworkPolicy>, // Open | Isolated | Proxy{url}
    pub isolate_pid: bool,
    pub extra: serde_json::Value,          // wrapper-specific opaque blob
}
```

`extra` is the escape hatch for oqto-specific knobs (oqto-guard config, eavs API key references) without coupling skdlr to oqto.

### Storage

- New nullable `sandbox_json` TEXT column on `schedules` table (crates/skdlr-core/src/storage.rs:49-161).
- Migration: ALTER TABLE add column with default NULL (matches existing in-band migration style).
- Round-trip via serde_json.

### Wrapper handoff

Replace argv placeholder substitution (backend/mod.rs:152-201) for sandbox-aware wrappers:

- If `Schedule.sandbox` is `Some`, write the spec + invocation context (schedule id, name, command, env, workdir) as JSON to a temp file, pass `--spec <path>` to the wrapper. Temp file is mode 0600, deleted after the wrapper exits.
- Alternative: pass JSON on stdin if the wrapper declares `wrapper_protocol = \"stdin\"` in config. Pick one and document.
- Keep the legacy placeholder mode for wrappers that don't declare a protocol, so existing `octo-sandbox` shims keep working.

### Config

Add to `ExecutorConfig`:
```toml
[executor]
wrapper = \"octo-sandbox\"
wrapper_protocol = \"spec_file\"  # spec_file | stdin | argv (legacy)
```

Drop `SKDLR_OCTO_MODE` once `wrapper_protocol` is set; deprecate with a warning for one release.

### CLI / API

- `skdlr add` accepts `--sandbox-profile`, `--deny-read`, `--allow-write`, `--isolate-network` flags.
- skdlr-api `POST /schedules` accepts a `sandbox` JSON object.
- `skdlr show` renders the spec.

## Non-goals

- skdlr does NOT enforce any sandbox rule itself. It serializes, persists, and hands off.
- No bwrap/seccomp code in skdlr.

## Definition of done

- `SandboxSpec` round-trips: CLI → storage → dispatcher → wrapper.
- New integration test: a fake wrapper script writes the received spec back to a file; the test asserts byte-for-byte equality.
- Existing wrappers without `wrapper_protocol` still work unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/sandbox-contract.md` describing the spec schema, file mode, protocol options, security expectations (wrapper trusted, spec is integrity-checked by file mode + parent dir).

title: runner_selector on Schedule + RemoteDispatcher trait impl
description:
Let a Schedule target a specific runner (or tag set) and dispatch there over a pluggable transport, instead of always running locally.

## Why

oqto already has remote runners: `RunnerHello` advertisement, runner_id routing, Unix socket / WebSocket transport, planned mTLS (oqto-e067) and SSH bootstrap (oqto-wdkj). skdlr's `Dispatcher` trait (crates/skdlr-core/src/dispatcher.rs:70-95) explicitly anticipates this with comments ("Future: HTTP-based dispatch to per-user runner agents") but only ships `LocalDispatcher`.

Without runner targeting, oqto can't schedule a job to run on a specific user's runner, on a remote host, or pinned to a machine class (gpu, build, etc.).

## What

### Schedule field

```rust
pub enum RunnerSelector {
    Local,
    RunnerId(Uuid),
    Tags(Vec<String>),       // any-of match against runner advertised tags
}
pub runner: RunnerSelector,  // defaults to Local
```

Persist as JSON column `runner_json` (or normalized `runner_kind`/`runner_value`).

### RemoteDispatcher

New impl of `Dispatcher` trait. Transport-agnostic via a `RunnerChannel` sub-trait:

```rust
trait RunnerChannel: Send + Sync {
    async fn dispatch(&self, runner: RunnerTarget, spec: JobSpec) -> Result<JobHandle>;
    async fn renew_lease(&self, h: &JobHandle) -> Result<()>;
    async fn cancel(&self, h: &JobHandle) -> Result<()>;
    async fn poll_status(&self, h: &JobHandle) -> Result<JobStatusUpdate>;
}
```

Ship one reference impl: `WsRunnerChannel` (WebSocket + JSON frames) so oqto can reuse its runner WS transport. mTLS config accepted via injected `rustls::ClientConfig` — skdlr ships no opinions about cert sources.

### Lease ownership across the wire

When a remote runner is executing a job, skdlr's lease must keep getting renewed. Two options — pick (a) for v1 simplicity:

(a) **Dispatcher-side heartbeat**: `RemoteDispatcher` task renews the lease in the local DB on a fixed cadence as long as `poll_status` reports Running. If the runner disappears, the heartbeat stops, the lease expires, the watchdog (vq7g.2) requeues. Document failure mode: a network partition where the runner is still working but unreachable will cause double-execution unless the runner side also checks an idempotency key.

(b) **Runner-side renew via callback**: runner calls back into skdlr-api `POST /jobs/:id/renew` with a lease token. Survives dispatcher crashes but adds a return path. Defer to v2.

### Runner registry

Minimal in skdlr-core: `RunnerRegistry` trait with `list()`, `get(id)`, `match_tags(tags)`. `LocalRunnerRegistry` is hardcoded (single Local). oqto plugs in its own that mirrors its RunnerHello state.

### CLI / API

- `skdlr add ... --runner <id>` or `--runner-tag gpu`
- `skdlr runners` lists known runners (delegates to registry)
- skdlr-api `GET /runners`, `POST /schedules` accepts `runner` field

## Dependencies

- skdlr-vq7g.2 (atomic lease claim/renew/requeue) MUST land first — heartbeat depends on `renew_lease()` semantics.

## Non-goals

- Inventing a new transport. Reuse oqto's WS frames; mirror, don't replace.
- Authentication policy. skdlr accepts a TLS config; the embedder owns identity.
- Cross-runner failover within a single dispatch (v2).

## Definition of done

- A schedule with `runner = RunnerId(x)` is dispatched to runner x via `WsRunnerChannel`.
- Lease is renewed for the duration of remote execution; killing the runner causes lease expiry → requeue.
- Integration test using an in-process fake runner.
- Docs: `docs/remote-runners.md` covering RunnerSelector semantics, lease ownership, partition behavior.

title: Per-job timeout and resource limits across backends
description:
Add `timeout_secs`, `cpu_quota`, `mem_limit_bytes`, `io_weight` to Schedule and enforce them across all four backends.

## Why

Today no backend enforces a per-job timeout. A runaway job holds a lease until the watchdog reaps it (vq7g.2), and resource starvation has to be solved out-of-band. oqto needs hard caps it can configure per schedule, especially for AI-agent jobs (Pi harness) where prompt loops can spin indefinitely.

## What

### Data model

Add to `Schedule`:
```rust
pub timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
pub cpu_quota: Option<f32>,        // 1.0 = one full core
pub mem_limit_bytes: Option<u64>,
pub io_weight: Option<u32>,        // 1..1000, systemd-style
```

Migration: nullable columns, default NULL.

### Backend mapping

| Backend  | timeout                          | cpu/mem/io                          |
|----------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| systemd  | `RuntimeMaxSec=` in .service     | `CPUQuota=`, `MemoryMax=`, `IOWeight=` |
| launchd  | `ExitTimeOut`/wrapper kill        | wrapper-only (launchd has no caps)  |
| schtasks | `/ET` end time + scheduled stop   | wrapper-only (Windows job objects)  |
| internal | `tokio::time::timeout` around child + SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation | `prlimit` on Linux, wrapper elsewhere |

Where the backend can't enforce natively (launchd cpu/mem, etc.), pass through to the wrapper via SandboxSpec (depends on the SandboxSpec issue).

### Internal backend specifics

In `crates/skdlr-core/src/backend/internal.rs:37-73`, wrap the child:
- `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(t), child.wait())`
- On expiry: send SIGTERM, wait `grace_period_secs` (default 10), then SIGKILL.
- Record terminal state in Run as `status = Failed`, `error = "timeout after Ns"`, distinct exit code (e.g., -1 with explicit error string).
- On Linux, apply `prlimit` via `nix` crate before exec for RLIMIT_CPU and RLIMIT_AS.

### Run record

Add `terminated_by: Option<TerminationReason>` (Timeout | Signal(i32) | Cancelled | Normal). Surface in `skdlr logs` output.

### CLI / API

- `skdlr add ... --timeout 300 --cpu-quota 0.5 --mem-limit 512MiB`
- skdlr-api accepts the new fields on POST/PATCH.

## Non-goals

- cgroup v2 manipulation for the internal backend on Linux (defer; rely on systemd or wrapper).
- Network bandwidth caps (use SandboxSpec network policy).

## Definition of done

- All four backends honor `timeout_secs` (with documented enforcement layer).
- Internal backend escalates SIGTERM → SIGKILL with grace period.
- Run.terminated_by populated correctly across normal/timeout/cancel paths.
- Tests: timeout fires, cleanup runs, lease released, retry counter incremented per JobInstance.max_attempts.

title: Secrets references decoupled from env map
description:
Add `secrets: Vec<SecretRef>` to Schedule so embedders (oqto + eavs) resolve secrets at exec time instead of skdlr persisting them in plaintext.

## Why

`Schedule.env` is `HashMap<String, String>` stored as plain JSON in SQLite. oqto today injects `EAVS_API_KEY` and provider keys this way — those land in `schedules.env` plaintext, in backups, in `skdlr show` output, in CLI argv if anyone ever templates them. The blast radius is wrong.

oqto manages secrets through eavs (LLM proxy with API keys). skdlr should hold a *reference*, not the secret.

## What

### Data model

```rust
pub struct SecretRef {
    pub env_var: String,                    // target env var name
    pub source: SecretSource,
}

pub enum SecretSource {
    Inline(String),                         // existing behavior, explicit opt-in
    EnvPassthrough(String),                 // read at exec from skdlr's env
    File { path: PathBuf, mode: SecretFileMode }, // mode validated (0600/0400)
    Provider { name: String, key: String }, // resolved by registered SecretProvider
}

pub trait SecretProvider: Send + Sync {
    async fn fetch(&self, key: &str) -> Result<SecretValue>;  // SecretValue zeroizes on drop
}
```

Add to Schedule:
```rust
pub secrets: Vec<SecretRef>,
```

### Resolution

Dispatcher resolves secrets just before exec:
1. Build env map starting from `Schedule.env` (non-sensitive only — recommend this becomes the rule).
2. For each `SecretRef`, fetch via the matching `SecretProvider`, set env var.
3. Pass the resolved env to the child process; never log it; never persist resolved values.

oqto registers an `EavsSecretProvider` that calls into eavs.

### Storage

`secrets_json` column. The persisted form NEVER contains resolved values, only refs. Add a CI lint (or unit test) that asserts no `SecretValue` ever serializes.

### CLI / API

- `skdlr add ... --secret EAVS_API_KEY=eavs:openai_default`
  - Parse `provider:key` to `SecretSource::Provider { name, key }`
  - `file:/path` → `SecretSource::File`
  - `env` → `SecretSource::EnvPassthrough`
- API mirrors. Inline secrets only via API with explicit `\"inline\": true` flag (so they can't slip in unintentionally).

### Display

`skdlr show` redacts: prints `EAVS_API_KEY = <provider:eavs:openai_default>` with no value.

## Non-goals

- Built-in vault. skdlr is a coordinator; embedders bring providers.
- Encryption-at-rest for inline secrets in v1 (document the risk; recommend providers).

## Definition of done

- `Schedule.env` documented as plaintext, non-sensitive only.
- `SecretProvider` trait + `EnvPassthroughProvider` and `FileProvider` ship in skdlr-core.
- Resolved secrets never appear in logs, Run records, or `skdlr show`.
- Test: a job with `Provider { name: \"test\", key: \"foo\" }` receives the resolved value as env, but the Schedule row in SQLite contains only the ref.

title: Live log streaming endpoint for JobInstance
description:
Stream stdout/stderr from a running JobInstance over SSE/WebSocket so oqto can show live output, not poll for `log_path` after the fact.

## Why

Today Run carries a `log_path` that's populated after the job finishes (when populated at all — the internal backend captures into `output.stdout`/`output.stderr` and where exactly that lands depends on the wrapper). oqto wants live output: its UI streams agent canonical events while jobs run, and a 5-minute backup job should not be a black box until it completes.

## What

### Capture model

Dispatcher writes line-buffered output to two places concurrently:
1. **Tail buffer**: ring buffer (e.g., last 64 KiB stdout + 64 KiB stderr) in memory keyed by `job_instance_id`, evicted on completion + drain.
2. **Persistent log file**: `~/.local/state/skdlr/logs/{job_instance_id}.log` (or `$STATE_DIR`), interleaved with stream tags (`O`/`E`/timestamp).

Update `Run.log_path` to point to the persistent file at completion. Keep the tail buffer alive for ~30s after completion so late subscribers can still read the trailing output.

### Streaming endpoint

skdlr-api adds:
- `GET /api/v1/tenants/:t/jobs/:id/logs/stream` — Server-Sent Events. Yields `{seq, ts, stream, text}` frames. Replays from a `?from_seq=N` cursor for reconnect.
- `GET /api/v1/tenants/:t/jobs/:id/logs` — historical fetch with `?tail=N` or `?since=ts`.

Why SSE over WebSocket: one-way, plays well with HTTP/2, easier to proxy. WebSocket wrapper can be added later if oqto needs bidirectional control on the same channel.

### Library surface

`skdlr-core` exposes:
```rust
trait LogSink: Send + Sync {
    fn append(&self, job_id: Uuid, frame: LogFrame);
}

trait LogStream {
    fn subscribe(&self, job_id: Uuid, from_seq: Option<u64>) -> BoxStream<LogFrame>;
    fn fetch(&self, job_id: Uuid, opts: FetchOpts) -> BoxStream<LogFrame>;
}
```

Default impl backs the tail buffer + file. Embedders (oqto) can swap in their own sink (e.g., to forward into eavs/hstry) by injecting at scheduler construction.

### Internal backend

Replace `Command::output()` (one-shot capture) with `Command::spawn()` + line-reader tasks on stdout/stderr. Pipe each line to `LogSink::append`. Final exit code recorded as today.

### Remote runner

When dispatching to a remote runner (skdlr-jrby.2), the runner streams log frames back over the same `RunnerChannel` and the dispatcher feeds them into the local LogSink. Frames carry the runner's seq numbers; the dispatcher rewrites to a contiguous local seq.

## Non-goals

- Structured log parsing (JSON line detection, ANSI handling). Keep it bytes.
- Long-term log storage / rotation policy. Document; let operators rotate `~/.local/state/skdlr/logs/`.
- Real-time tailing of historical jobs. The stream endpoint covers running + recently-completed only.

## Definition of done

- Internal backend writes per-line frames to LogSink while the job runs.
- SSE endpoint streams new frames in real time and supports `from_seq` resume.
- `skdlr logs <name> --follow` uses the streaming API.
- Test: spawn a job that prints lines on a timer, subscribe mid-run, assert all frames arrive in order with no gaps and no duplicates.

title: Migrate oqto integration from CLI scraping to skdlr-core library
description:
Replace oqto's text parsing of `skdlr` CLI output with direct use of `skdlr-core` (preferred) or stabilized `skdlr-api`. This is the prerequisite for every other child of this epic.

## Why

oqto_refactor backend/crates/oqto/src/api/handlers/misc.rs:200-400 implements `exec_skdlr_command()`, `scheduler_overview()`, `scheduler_delete()` etc. by `tokio::process::Command::new(\"skdlr\")` and parsing stdout for "list" and "next" output formats. Problems:

- Any CLI output change in skdlr breaks oqto silently.
- New fields (sandbox, runner, timeout, secrets, structured logs from this epic) cannot be expressed in line-oriented CLI output without churn.
- Errors are stringified, losing typed error context.
- Performance: a fork+exec per query.

## What

### Decision: library or API

Default to **library** (skdlr-core as a crate dependency) because:
- oqto is Rust; no language barrier.
- skdlr-core is already public (lib.rs:9-27) and exposes Storage, Scheduler, Backend trait, models.
- One process, shared SQLite via WAL mode.
- API can stay on for non-Rust embedders.

Use **skdlr-api** only if oqto's deployment topology requires skdlr to live in another process (e.g., container boundary). If so, generate a typed Rust client from the OpenAPI/handler set and version it.

### Migration steps

1. Add `skdlr-core = { path = \"...\" }` to oqto's backend workspace.
2. Build a thin `oqto::scheduler` module wrapping skdlr-core: `list()`, `get(name)`, `create(spec)`, `delete(name)`, `pause/resume`, `runs(name)`, `next_runs()`. Same shape as today's HTTP handlers, typed inputs/outputs.
3. Replace each call site in `misc.rs` to use the wrapper. Keep the HTTP handler shape unchanged for the frontend.
4. Delete `exec_skdlr_command` and the parsing code.
5. Remove the `skdlr` binary as a runtime dependency for the oqto backend (still useful for ops/CLI).

### Compatibility

- Storage path: oqto opens the same SQLite file skdlr CLI writes to. Confirm WAL semantics under multi-process access (skdlr-core uses WAL, foreign_keys=ON — should be safe). Document the expectation in `docs/embedding.md`.
- Tenant id: oqto picks a tenant_id per user; document the convention.

### Stabilization checklist for skdlr-core public surface

- Re-export `Storage`, `Scheduler`, `SchedulerConfig`, `Backend`, `Schedule`, `Run`, `JobInstance`, `Dispatcher`, `LocalDispatcher`, `Config`. (Most already exposed; audit lib.rs.)
- Mark non-public-surface modules `pub(crate)`.
- Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to public enums likely to grow (ScheduleStatus, JobState).
- Bump skdlr-core to 0.x with a CHANGELOG.

## Dependencies / sequencing

This issue MUST land before skdlr-jrby.1 / .2 / .3 / .5 actually ship value to oqto. The new fields (SandboxSpec, runner_selector, timeout, log streaming) all assume a typed boundary; bolting them onto CLI parsing would be wasted work.

Order: `.6 → .1 / .3 → .2 → .5` (and `.4 secrets` slots in anywhere after `.6`).

## Definition of done

- oqto compiles with skdlr-core dependency, no `skdlr` binary spawned at runtime.
- All scheduler HTTP handlers in oqto are backed by typed library calls.
- Integration test: oqto creates a schedule via library, skdlr CLI sees it, runs fire as expected.
- `docs/embedding.md` covers: SQLite path, tenant_id convention, WAL safety, version compatibility.

title: Systemd backend emits invalid OnCalendar for stepped cron fields
description: Dogfood repro: skdlr add oqto-pi-runtime-update --schedule '17 */6 * * *' persists the schedule but generates OnCalendar=*-*-* */6:17:00. systemd rejects it ('Failed to parse calendar specification'; timer bad-setting), while valid systemd syntax is *-*-* 0/6:17:00. Fix cron_to_oncalendar to translate wildcard step expressions by field (minute/hour start at 0; day/month at 1 where supported), add regressions for stepped hours and minutes, and prove generated timer passes systemd-analyze calendar/verify and can be enabled. Ensure add does not report a usable enabled schedule when backend activation fails.
close_reason: Fixed cron wildcard-step conversion to valid systemd start/step syntax. Regression covers stepped hour/minute/date fields and zero-step rejection. Real timer proof: OnCalendar=*-*-* 0/6:17:00 passes systemd-analyze verify, enabled successfully, and reports next trigger at 12:17.

title: systemd timer-triggered runs are not recorded in skdlr run history
close_reason: Implemented systemd journal parsing in backend.get_runs and updated CLI logs to merge DB + backend history, so timer-triggered runs appear.

title: systemd service files missing ExecStart= prefix
description:
## Bug Summary

skdlr v0.2.1 generates invalid systemd service unit files. The "ExecStart=" directive prefix is missing from the generated `[Service]` section, causing systemd to reject the unit with "bad unit file setting".

## Environment

- skdlr version: 0.2.1
- OS: Arch Linux
- Backend: systemd (user)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run: `skdlr add "test" --schedule "0 * * * *" --command "date"`
2. Observe error: `Unit skdlr-test.service has a bad unit file setting`
3. Check generated file at `~/.config/systemd/user/skdlr-test.service`

## Actual Behavior

Generated service file contains:
```ini
[Service]
Type=oneshot
/bin/sh -c '/bin/sh -c exec date'
```

Note: `/bin/sh -c ...` appears on its own line without the `ExecStart=` prefix.

## Expected Behavior

Generated service file should contain:
```ini
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/bin/sh -c exec date'
```

## Workaround

Manually edit the generated `.service` file to add `ExecStart=` before the command, then run `systemctl --user daemon-reload`.

## Root Cause

Likely in the service file template/rendering code — the command string is being written to the service file without the `ExecStart=` key.
close_reason: Fixed: Added ExecStart= prefix in render_exec_start() in backend/mod.rs and also in the fallback code in systemd.rs

title: Durable Execution v1 (SQLite, step checkpoints, lease-safe workers)
description:
Adopt an Absurd-inspired durable execution model in skdlr while staying SQLite-first per user/workspace DB.

Reference
- ../external-repos/absurd @ 3120ce9

Goals
- Multi-step job execution with durable checkpoints.
- Lease-safe worker claims and watchdog recovery hardened for production.
- Idempotent step transitions and replay-safe retries.
- Keep architecture compatible with optional future Postgres backend without requiring it now.

Scope
1) Data model
   - job_instances durable state machine
   - step checkpoint table with idempotency keys
2) Scheduler/runtime
   - atomic claim+lease semantics
   - lease renewal, stuck-job requeue, deterministic retry backoff
3) APIs/UX
   - expose per-step status and resume point in CLI/API/TUI
4) Verification
   - crash/restart recovery tests
   - contention tests on SQLite WAL + busy_timeout
   - invariant checks for state transitions

Definition of done
- jobs can resume from last successful step after crash
- no duplicate side effects when retries happen (idempotency enforced)
- watchdog recovers expired leases without manual intervention
- docs updated with durable execution semantics and operational guidance
